properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud 2026-08-24, reconsidering redb after raising it the same day. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

HIS WORDS: *"I was thinking about going to redb, but after thinking about it, I'm starting to think about scalability, particularly if my brother and I move forward with flo2... let's say flo2 has 10000+ users (either collaborating on the same project OR each having their own project)... While the redb and others may compile faster, I'm concerned that they won't scale like rocksdb can. rocksdb was built to support huge amounts of data, so I'm thinking about sticking with it. That being said, there are alternate ways to do things. Maybe we stand up a redb db just for a session and the reflow.json file becomes the enduring thing between each session (may have to make safeguards to ensure that the reflow2 graph is exported at the conclusion of each session). There could be multiple iterations of this that get around using the db as the enduring/persistent storage of the graph and instead switching to making the reflow2.json object file the enduring piece?"*

⭐⭐ THE SHARP PART, AND IT IS HIS: HIS TWO WORRIES DISSOLVE EACH OTHER RATHER THAN TRADING OFF. The redb question was "which store compiles faster"; the scale question is "which store survives 10k tenants". Those look like a straight trade until the store stops being durable. **If the store is a per-session cache derived from the export, then neither property is being chosen at the same altitude any more:** durability and scale move to the export/object layer, and the embedded engine is judged only on hydrate-and-query speed for ONE design — which is small. reflow2's own design is the largest one anybody has, and it is 3,142 nodes / 8.4 MB. A store that "does not scale like RocksDB" is not being asked to.

🛑 AND HE HAS ARRIVED HERE BEFORE, FROM A DIFFERENT DIRECTION — WHICH IS EVIDENCE, NOT DUPLICATION. `dec:idea-a-hosted-tier-of-many-single-writer-tenants` (2026-08-09) already records this as its FIFTH ROAD, in almost the same words: *"OBJECT STORAGE HOLDS THE EXPORT AS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH, a node HYDRATES a RocksDB+tantivy cache on demand, and eviction is free because the cache is derived... reflow2 already has the primitive: the export is deterministic, sorted, content-hashed and self-contained — that IS a per-tenant blob, and the store is already derived rather than authoritative."* Two independent derivations two weeks apart, from a hosting question and from a compile-speed question, landing on one shape. READ IN FULL AND JUDGED DISTINCT rather than merged (`distinct_from`), because the reasons differ and both matter.

WHAT IS NEW HERE, over the 2026-08-09 record — the grounds on which it was kept separate:
1. **THE GRANULARITY IS THE SESSION, NOT THE TENANT.** The fifth road hydrates per tenant on demand, as part of a hosted tier. This proposes the store's lifetime be a SESSION — the same mechanism aimed at a smaller unit, and it applies to the LOCAL single-user case where there is no tenancy at all. That matters because **it is testable today, on one laptop, with no flo2 and no hosting decision.** The fifth road cannot be tried until somebody builds a tier.
2. **IT MAKES THE BACKEND CHOICE REVERSIBLE RATHER THAN CORRECT.** If the store is derived, picking wrong costs a re-hydrate, not a migration. `dec:absorb-rocksdb-024-unchanged-then-switch-separately` and the redb question both get cheaper, and the rust-rocksdb switch stops being a one-way door.
3. **IT NAMES THE SAFEGUARD AS PART OF THE IDEA** — recorded separately, because "what is the enduring artifact" and "what makes the enduring artifact reliable" are answered by different work.

⚠️ THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, RECORDED BESIDE THE IDEA RATHER THAN USED TO ARGUE IT DOWN. The prior node measured the thing that bites: **~9x inflation from export to store** (its figures: 1,828 nodes = 3.8 MB export = 33 MB store, RocksDB plus the tantivy index), and it flagged that `shared.rs` budgets **30 seconds for a cold open**. If hydrate-and-index is seconds rather than milliseconds, "a store per session" turns every session start into that cost — and the local single-user case, the one that works well today, pays it for a benefit only the hosted case collects. **That is the risk this idea has to clear, and it is measurable rather than arguable.**

📌 ONE DATA POINT TAKEN TODAY, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. Opening reflow2's own 3,142-node RocksDB store cold, to a served MCP `initialize`, measured **2.4 seconds** (2026-08-24, after `--stop-shared`). ⚠️ THAT IS NOT THE HYDRATE NUMBER: it opens an EXISTING store with its tantivy index already built, which is the cheap half. The measurement the prior node asks for — import an 8.4 MB export to first query, index included — has still not been taken, and it is the one that decides this.

🛑 WHAT NOBODY HAS CHECKED, and it is the way this fails LATE rather than early: whether a session hydrated from an export can still answer the questions that depend on ACCUMULATED STORE STATE rather than on the design — the confirmation ledger's dates, drift baselines, `write_gen`, the sidecar identity files (`.id.json`, `.sync.json`). The export is self-contained about the DESIGN; that it is self-contained about everything a running seat believes is a DIFFERENT claim, and nobody has tested it.

RECORDED AS A QUESTION, NOT A CONCLUSION. Nothing here says the weld should be loosened; it says the trade Anthony thought he was facing may not be one.
properties.name: RULED 2026-09-11 — REJECTED by its own condition: accepted "conditional on Decision 1", and Decision 1 went the other way. The store stays durable; there is no per-session cache to make the export the truth
properties.rationale:
RULED BY ANTHONY, 2026-09-11. His word on this node was *"accept, conditional on 1"* — and Decision 1 (`dec:idea-does-reflow2-need-a-byte-store-at-all-or-only-durability`) was then ruled the other way: the store STAYS, RocksDB kept and shipped as a release binary. The condition failed, so this is rejected by implication rather than on its own merits, and that distinction is the record.

WHAT SURVIVES OF IT, because the reasoning was sound and should not be lost with the status: the observation that the flo2 10k-tenant scaling worry and the compile-time worry dissolve each other once durability moves to the object layer is still true — it just no longer needs THIS mechanism to be true, because `dec:idea-what-guarantees-the-export-if-the-export-is-the-only-durable-copy` was ACCEPTED the same day and moves the export to the server regardless. The git record becomes reliable without the store becoming ephemeral.

⚠️ NOT REJECTED FOR A HOSTED TIER. This ruling is about one person on one laptop with a prebuilt binary, where the store's cost is the builder's and its benefit is the user's. `dec:idea-a-hosted-tier-of-many-single-writer-tenants` and `dec:idea-where-does-the-10k-work-actually-land` stay open, and the session-cache shape may be right THERE — eviction and export as one event was the strongest argument on this node and it was never answered, only made unnecessary for the laptop case.
